claim_text: Reduced kidney function can impair potassium excretion and increase the risk of hyperkalemia; potassium supplementation in people with kidney disease should therefore be based on clinical indication, laboratory results and medication review rather than assumed need.
health_goal_or_outcome: Prevent unsafe potassium supplementation in people with impaired renal potassium handling.

population.age_range: All ages; kidney function and reference ranges vary.
population.sex_or_life_stage: All life stages; pregnancy requires specific review.
population.health_status: People with chronic kidney disease or impaired renal function.
population.other_context: Medication use and serum potassium are key modifiers.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Potassium supplements, electrolyte products and potassium-based salt substitutes.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Potassium Health Professional Fact Sheet describes potassium balance and hyperkalemia risk in kidney disease and with relevant medications.
limitations: Kidney disease severity varies; this is not a blanket dietary potassium restriction.
Serum potassium and eGFR are required for individualized clinical decisions.
Do not advise stopping prescribed medicines.
